retention.value: Kept as a checkpoint on the platform; no reaping period published. A failed resume leaves the sandbox paused with its checkpoint.

retention.value: Disk deleted immediately; only Persistent Volume files and snapshots survive

hermes.route: not found as a one-click or documented route. A sandbox can host it manually: create a sandbox (dashboard, CLI or SDK), install Hermes Agent in its terminal, keep the process running, and expose its port.
hermes.officialTemplateOrGuide: not found: the template catalog lists only n8n, Grafana and OpenClaw
hermes.manualSteps: 1) Create a sandbox (dashboard New Sandbox, or `lizard sandbox create`). 2) Open the Terminal tab. 3) Install Hermes Agent and its runtime. 4) Add the model key. 5) Run it as a long-lived process. 6) exposePort for its web UI. 7) Pause or kill it when done; use a Persistent Volume for files.
hermes.nonCoderFromDashboard: Partly. The dashboard can create a sandbox and open a terminal without code, but the Hermes install itself is typed commands; there is no guided template.

quotes.quote: The dashboard lets you create and manage Sandboxes without code.
The Terminal tab opens a shell in a running sandbox.

openclaw.route: One-click template on the app platform: Deploy OpenClaw provisions the gateway, generates an auth token, and gives it a public HTTPS domain.
openclaw.manualSteps: Click Deploy Now, wait for the build, then read the generated gateway token from Dashboard → Logs and open the HTTPS domain.
openclaw.nonCoderFromDashboard: Yes. The template is deployed from the browser; no terminal is required to get it running.

quotes.quote: On Lizard, all of the above happens when you click Deploy — the database is provisioned and its credentials are wired into the app's environment automatically.
This template's startup script generates a random gateway token on boot and prints it to the deploy logs, so it comes up reachable and authenticated on the first try.
